title: SQL Dialects and Portability Principles
learningObjectives: Explain why SQL syntax and behaviour vary among database products.
Identify common portability differences in types, functions, pagination and identity columns.
Choose a target DBMS and version before relying on product-specific syntax.
Use portable SQL constructs when they meet the requirement.
Explain why SQLite validation alone does not prove compatibility with server DBMS products.

understand.concept: SQL is standardized, but database products implement different dialects, data types, functions, transaction features and administrative commands. Portable SQL uses common syntax where practical and isolates product-specific behaviour behind tested, documented boundaries.
understand.whyItMatters: A query that works in SQLite may not run unchanged in MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server or Access. Knowing the dialect prevents incorrect assumptions during development and migration.
understand.analogy: SQL portability is like translating a precise instruction into several product dialects: the intent stays the same, but the exact words and rules can differ.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not model type systems, function return types, time-zone rules, optimizer behaviour or transaction semantics.

explain.narrative:
## SQL standard and product dialects
SQL standards define common language features, but database products add extensions and differ in implementation details. SQLite is an embedded database library; MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server commonly run as database servers; Access has its own SQL and application model.

## Common portability differences
Differences include identity columns, data types, date arithmetic, string concatenation, NULL functions, pagination, transaction behaviour, DDL support and parameter-binding APIs. Identifier quoting and reserved words can also vary.

## A practical portability strategy
Choose a target DBMS, document the dialect for each runnable example, use portable constructs such as COALESCE when appropriate, and isolate product-specific code. Test queries against the actual engine and version used in production; SQLite success does not prove server-database compatibility.

questions.prompt: Does a query passing in SQLite prove it works in PostgreSQL?
options: No, dialect and behaviour differences must be tested
Only if the query uses uppercase keywords
Only if the table has a primary key
questions.answer: No, dialect and behaviour differences must be tested
questions.explanation: SQLite validation is not proof of compatibility with other database engines.

questions.prompt: Which feature commonly differs among database products?
options: The meaning of a table name
questions.explanation: Identity, date/time, NULL and pagination syntax often differ.

questions.prompt: What is a good portability strategy?
options: Choose a target engine, document dialect-specific code and test against it
Assume SQLite is the same as every server DBMS
questions.answer: Choose a target engine, document dialect-specific code and test against it
questions.explanation: Portability requires explicit target selection and verification.

questions.prompt: Which function is commonly used for portable NULL fallback?
questions.explanation: COALESCE is widely supported for returning the first non-NULL expression.
